evidence_refs.description: HTTPServer.wait now loops around sleep without handling KeyboardInterrupt.
The base implementation caught KeyboardInterrupt and broke out of the wait loop cleanly.
The server advertises CTRL+C as its normal quit mechanism and run() directly calls server.wait().

findings.technical_rationale: Removing the KeyboardInterrupt handler changes the synchronous run() shutdown path: pressing CTRL+C still unwinds the server context, but KeyboardInterrupt now escapes run() and ordinarily produces an exception traceback instead of returning normally. This is an unrelated user-visible regression in the same PR, not part of the clean client-disconnect fix.
findings.comment_usefulness_rationale: A comment is actionable because the prior try/except can be retained while the parser readiness changes remain intact, preserving the documented interactive shutdown behavior.

review_summary: The parser readiness change is internally consistent across synchronous and asynchronous implementations and addresses clean disconnects before a request starts. One separate low-severity regression was found: the synchronous server no longer absorbs CTRL+C in its documented wait path. Local tests could not be executed because pytest is not installed, but the finding follows deterministically from the base/head control flow.
